open_points.subject: A11 attempt tracing semantics
open_points.text: "So every attempt has exactly one concluding NodeExecution M23 with its number; ... and an attempt whose unknown outcome the owner resolves `applied` has one more NodeExecution with the same number"
open_points.question: For one attempt resolved from `outcome_unknown` to `applied`, is there exactly one NodeExecution total or two (original `outcome_unknown` plus resolution record), and which one is considered the attempt's concluding record?
options: Exactly one record per attempt (replace or reinterpret the first record)
Two records for that attempt number (`outcome_unknown`, then resolution record), with the second being the conclusion
open_points.default_guess: Two records for the same attempt number, second one treated as final conclusion.

open_points.subject: EffectApproval lifecycle when run ends without using/deciding all approvals
open_points.text: A10: "When a run ends, its undecided and unused approvals can no longer be decided or used." M24 statuses are only `requested`, `approved`, `refused`, `used`.
open_points.question: When a run ends (`failed`, `refused`, `cancelled`, `succeeded`) and approvals are still `requested` or `approved`, do their statuses stay as-is forever, or must they transition to a terminal status?
options: Keep `requested`/`approved` unchanged but enforce 'cannot decide/use' by rule
Introduce/derive a terminal expired/closed condition at run end
open_points.default_guess: Keep existing status and enforce non-usable/non-decidable by run-ended checks.

open_points.subject: Agent redaction for personal-data files and file references
open_points.text: A07 rule 4 says: "An agent never receives a `personal_data` value ... it returns only the value's digest and class ... and no `value_id`." A10 preview includes file digest/size/media type; M22 and M23 include file facts.
open_points.question: Does the personal-data redaction rule apply only to StoredValue payloads, or also to file-related trace/preview fields (spooled-file facts, media type, size, identifiers) when the file class is `personal_data`?
options: Redact only value payloads/`value_id`; file metadata may still be shown
Redact file references similarly (digest/class only, or stricter) for personal-data files
open_points.default_guess: Allow file metadata already listed by rules (digest/size/media type), but never bytes.

open_points.subject: Content-identity normalization for unordered logical collections
open_points.text: A01: identities are computed from meaning facts via canonical JSON; e.g., `flow_version_id` from `inputs`, `outputs`, `nodes`, `edges`, `constants` (M13), and contract/ports similarly.
open_points.question: When logically equivalent content is submitted with different list ordering (e.g., node list, edge list, port list), must identity treat them as equal (normalize order) or different (order-significant)?
options: Order-significant arrays: different order => different identity
Normalize/sort collections before hashing so equivalent sets share identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat submitted array order as significant unless an explicit normalization rule is added.

open_points.subject: `corpus_digest` definition for admission reuse
open_points.text: M08: "`corpus_digest`: the digest of the corpus the verdict covered"; A04 reuses verdict when one exists for implementation and "current corpus digest."
open_points.question: What exact canonical structure is hashed to produce `corpus_digest` (e.g., ordered list of `trial_case_id`, full case content, inclusion of expected outputs, fixtures), so two implementations compute the same digest?
options: Digest ordered list of trial_case_id in corpus order
Digest canonical JSON of full active-case contents in corpus order
open_points.default_guess: Digest the ordered list of trial_case_id values in corpus order.

open_points.subject: Mapped node trace shape for non-empty lists
open_points.text: A13 rule 6 defines a special single NodeExecution for an empty mapped list; A15 says every concluded attempt at an element writes one NodeExecution.
open_points.question: For a non-empty mapped node, is trace only per-element NodeExecution (`map_index` set), or also one aggregate node-level NodeExecution summarizing mapped-node conclusion?
options: Per-element records plus an aggregate summary record
open_points.default_guess: Per-element records only; no extra aggregate NodeExecution.
